claim.pdf_says: READ statement, Format 1 (sequential): the AT END / NOT AT END group is printed as a tall BRACKET with a pair of vertical CHOICE-INDICATOR BARS just inside it, spanning both stacked alternatives:  [|  AT END imperative-statement-1  |]  /  [|  NOT AT END imperative-statement-2  |]
claim.markdown_says:
[ [ AT END imperative-statement-1         ] ]
  [ [ NOT AT END imperative-statement-2     ] ]
[ END-READ ]
claim.why_it_matters: Per 5.2.6.4 a pair of vertical bars just inside a BRACKET means zero or more of the enclosed alternatives may be specified, each at most once, in any order - so AT END and NOT AT END may BOTH appear on the same READ. The markdown replaced the bars with a nested bracket; under the transcription's own convention (a tall delimiter is written by repeating it on every row - cf. the { NEXT } / { PREVIOUS } and [ WITH LOCK ] / [ WITH NO LOCK ] groups in the same figure) that reads as bracket-inside-bracket, i.e. AT MOST ONE of AT END / NOT AT END. That is falsely restrictive and would make legal COBOL look illegal. It also contradicts GR 13 c on page 726, which describes control passing to imperative-statement-2 of a NOT AT END phrase on a statement that also carries an AT END phrase. The rest of the document uses bars for this construct (e.g. specs/ISO_COBOL.md:26324 '| NOT INVALID KEY imperative-statement-2 |', :25475 'NOT ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-2' enclosed in bars).

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by direct inspection of the rendered glyphs. I rendered PDF page 722 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v722/spec_p722.png) and magnified the AT END delimiters to 8x (crop_leftdelim.png / crop_rightdelim.png). LEFT delimiter: an outer '[' - a vertical stem with short horizontal feet projecting RIGHT at top and bottom - and immediately inboard of it a TALLER, BARE vertical stroke with NO feet at either end. RIGHT delimiter: mirror image - a bare footless vertical stroke, then a ']' whose feet project LEFT. A footless vertical stroke inboard of a footed bracket is a choice-indicator bar, not a second bracket. The control comparison is decisive: the WITH LOCK / WITH NO LOCK group four lines above in the SAME figure (crop_withlock.png) shows a single footed '[' and a single footed ']' with nothing inboard. The printed page therefore reads [| AT END imperative-statement-1 |] / [| NOT AT END imperative-statement-2 |]. The markdown at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:29464-29465 reads '[ [ AT END imperative-statement-1 ] ]' / '[ [ NOT AT END imperative-statement-2 ] ]' - no bar glyph anywhere, and no figure note flagging choice indicators.

The meaning genuinely changes. The transcription quotes both rules itself: 5.2.6.2 (line 2693) - brackets indicate 'the syntax element contained within the brackets OR ONE OF THE ALTERNATIVES contained within the brackets may be explicitly specified'; 5.2.6.4 (line 2703) - 'Choice indicators are a pair of bars, |, that enclose a portion of a general format. ... When enclosed by brackets, ZERO OR MORE of the alternatives contained within the choice indicators shall be specified, but any single alternative may be specified only once. ... The alternatives may be specified in any order.' Nested plain brackets around a two-row stack therefore license AT MOST ONE of AT END / NOT AT END; the printed bracket-plus-bars licenses BOTH on one READ, in either order. Rejecting 'READ f AT END ... NOT AT END ... END-READ' would reject universally legal COBOL.

I also ruled out the standard refutations. (a) Not reflow/wrapping/page furniture - this is a substituted delimiter glyph on the same line. (b) Not an alternate house notation for bars - the transcription renders this exact construct WITH bars in dozens of places (25478, 25494, 25508, 25699, 25736, 26327, 26510, 26639, 29820, 30097) and even carries explicit '(ISO 5.2.6.4)' figure notes explaining that plain brackets without bars 'would wrongly read as zero-or-one' (e.g. the ADD Format 1 note, and CALL Format 2 at 25741). Page 722 has no such note. (c) The claim does not misquote either source - both quoted strings match byte-for-byte what I read.

One part of the claim's supporting argument is weaker than stated and should not be relied on: page 726 GR 13 c (line 29614) says only 'Control is transferred to the end of the READ statement, or, if the NOT AT END phrase or NOT INVALID KEY phrase is specified, to imperative-statement-2' - it does not explicitly describe a READ carrying BOTH phrases. The finding stands entirely on the printed glyphs plus 5.2.6.4; the GR 13 c corroboration is at best indirect. The claim is also INCOMPLETE: the identical defect appears a second time on the same page in Format 2 (random), where the PDF likewise prints [| INVALID KEY imperative-statement-3 |] / [| NOT INVALID KEY imperative-statement-4 |] (verified in crop_invalid.png - same footless inner strokes) but the markdown at 29483-29484 writes '[ [ INVALID KEY imperative-statement-3 ] ]' / '[ [ NOT INVALID KEY imperative-statement-4 ] ]'. Both occurrences must be fixed together.
verdict.corrected_description:
Page 722, 14.9.30.2 READ statement general formats - the transcription drops the CHOICE-INDICATOR BARS from BOTH exception-phrase groups on the page, replacing each bar with a second bracket.

Format 1 (sequential), specs/ISO_COBOL.md:29464-29465. PDF prints a tall bracket with a pair of footless vertical bars just inside it, spanning both stacked alternatives:
  [|  AT END imperative-statement-1      |]
  [|  NOT AT END imperative-statement-2  |]
Markdown has '[ [ AT END imperative-statement-1 ] ]' / '[ [ NOT AT END imperative-statement-2 ] ]'.

Format 2 (random), specs/ISO_COBOL.md:29483-29484 - SAME defect, not mentioned in the original claim. PDF prints:
  [|  INVALID KEY imperative-statement-3      |]
  [|  NOT INVALID KEY imperative-statement-4  |]
Markdown has '[ [ INVALID KEY imperative-statement-3 ] ]' / '[ [ NOT INVALID KEY imperative-statement-4 ] ]'.

Evidence that the inner strokes are bars, not brackets: at 8x the inner vertical strokes are taller than the outer delimiters and have NO horizontal feet at top or bottom, whereas the outer '[' and ']' have feet - and the WITH LOCK / WITH NO LOCK group in the same figure, a genuine plain bracket, shows a single footed delimiter on each side with nothing inboard.

Normative impact: per 5.2.6.4, bars enclosed by brackets mean zero or more of the enclosed alternatives, each at most once, in any order - so one READ may carry BOTH AT END and NOT AT END (Format 1), or BOTH INVALID KEY and NOT INVALID KEY (Format 2), in either order. Per 5.2.6.2, the transcribed nested plain brackets read as at most one alternative, which is falsely restrictive and would reject legal COBOL.

Fix: render both groups in the house choice-indicator style already used throughout the file, e.g.
  ⎡|  AT END imperative-statement-1      |⎤
  ⎣|  NOT AT END imperative-statement-2  |⎦
and add a '**Figure notes (ISO 5.2.6.4)**' annotation of the kind attached to the ADD Format 1 and CALL Format 2 figures.

Caveat on the original rationale: the cited page-726 GR 13 c does not actually describe a READ carrying both an AT END and a NOT AT END phrase - it only says control passes to imperative-statement-2 when a NOT AT END / NOT INVALID KEY phrase is specified. The finding rests on the printed glyphs and 5.2.6.4, not on GR 13 c.
